## Claims
- [source-backed] The 2024 paper defines integral \(\Lambda\), \(I_{r,n-r}\), \(\overline\Lambda=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and states Theorem 1.2: for every bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(J_v\) is minimally generated by \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-110]
- [source-backed] In the Grassmannian model, \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) corresponds to \(i^j\), and \(r\)-Grassmannian Bruhat containment is Young-diagram containment; the integral quotient has Schur basis indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 779-834; lines 847-862]
- [proved] The requested target is established: both original Theorem-4.8 families are minimal generators of the actual integral ideal \(J_v\), including \(i=n-r\) or \(j=r\).

## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\). The original hypotheses are
\[
1\le t\le r,s\le n,\qquad t>r+s-n.
\]
Thus
\[
1\le i=s-t+1\le q,\qquad 1\le j=r-t+1\le r,
\]
because \(t\ge r+s-n+1\). Hence \(p=q-i,c=r-j\ge0\), and
\[
a=\min(p,c),\qquad b=\min(i,j).
\]

Define
\[
I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda,\qquad
A_{r,q}=\Lambda/I_{r,q}.
\]
Littlewood–Richardson containment \(c_{\lambda,\nu}^{\rho}\ne0\Rightarrow
\lambda,\nu\subseteq\rho\) shows that \(I_{r,q}\) is an ideal. Therefore
\[
A_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda.
\]
The Grassmannian Bruhat identification in the cited source gives
\[
J_v=\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda.
\tag{1}
\]
This is an ideal: multiplying \(\bar s_\lambda\) with \(i^j\subseteq\lambda\) by any Schur class yields only surviving LR terms \(\bar s_\rho\) with \(\lambda\subseteq\rho\), hence \(i^j\subseteq\rho\).

For integrality of transpose, let
\[
H(z)=\sum_{m\ge0}h_mz^m,\qquad E(z)=\sum_{m\ge0}e_mz^m,
\qquad H(z)E(-z)=1.
\]
Coefficient comparison recursively gives \(e_m\in\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_m]\). Thus
\(\omega(h_m)=e_m\) defines an integral endomorphism of
\(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\). Applying \(\omega\) to
\(H(z)E(-z)=1\) gives \(\omega(e_m)=h_m\), so \(\omega^2=1\).
Jacobi–Trudi and dual Jacobi–Trudi give
\[
s_\lambda=\det(h_{\lambda_u-u+v}),\qquad
s_{\lambda'}=\det(e_{\lambda_u-u+v}),
\]
and consequently
\[
\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\quad\text{integrally.}
\tag{2}
\]

Since \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\), (2) gives
\[
\bar\omega_{r,q}:A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r},
\qquad \bar s_\lambda\longmapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
i^j\subseteq\lambda
\iff \lambda_u\ge i\ (1\le u\le j)
\iff \lambda'_v\ge j\ (1\le v\le i)
\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda'.
\]
Applying this basiswise to (1) proves the equality of actual ideals
\[
\bar\omega_{r,q}(J_v)
=
\bigoplus_{\,j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q}\mathbb Z\bar s_\nu.
\tag{3}
\]

Set
\[
r^\dagger=q,\qquad s^\dagger=n-s,\qquad
t^\dagger=n-r-s+t.
\]
All transformed bigrassmannian inequalities hold:
\[
t^\dagger\ge1
\quad\text{from }t>r+s-n;
\]
\[
t^\dagger\le r^\dagger\iff t\le s,\qquad
t^\dagger\le s^\dagger\iff t\le r;
\]
\[
t^\dagger>r^\dagger+s^\dagger-n
\iff t>0.
\]
Also \(r^\dagger,s^\dagger\ge1\): \(r=n\) would force \(t>s\), contradicting
\(t\le s\), and \(s=n\) similarly contradicts \(t\le r\). Hence
\(v^\dagger=v_{r^\dagger,s^\dagger,t^\dagger,n}\) is bigrassmannian. Its parameters are
\[
i^\dagger=j,\quad j^\dagger=i,\quad
a^\dagger=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\quad b^\dagger=b.
\]
Thus the right side of (3) is precisely \(J_{v^\dagger}\).

Theorem 1.2 applied to \(v\) proves minimality of
\[
\mathcal F_{\rm down}
=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}.
\]
Applied to \(v^\dagger\), it proves minimality of
\[
\mathcal F^\dagger_{\rm down}
=\{\bar s_\nu:j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}.
\]
Transpose bijects this latter family with
\[
\mathcal F_{\rm right}
=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},
\]
because
\[
(j^i,b^a)'=((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}).
\]
By (3), \(\bar\omega_{r,q}\) identifies their generated ideals. If a proper
subfamily of \(\mathcal F_{\rm right}\) generated \(J_v\), its transpose would
be a proper generating subfamily of \(\mathcal F^\dagger_{\rm down}\), contrary
to Theorem 1.2. Hence \(\mathcal F_{\rm right}\) is minimal.

Finally, \(a=0\) iff \(i=q\) or \(j=r\). Then
\[
(i^j,b^0)=i^j=((i+0)^b,i^{j-b}),
\]
so both families are the singleton \(\{\bar s_{i^j}\}\). This class is nonzero
because \(i^j\subseteq q^r\). The transformed tuple remains bigrassmannian and
also has \(a^\dagger=0\); hence the preceding Theorem-1.2 and transpose argument
includes both boundary cases.

- None relative to the supplied 2024 theorem passage and the stated integral symmetric-function identities.
